q: The RBI has a statutory right to inspect any bank.
opts: It depends on the bank type
exp: RBI has the right to inspect any bank under the Banking Regulation Act.

q: A banker's first duty is to preserve the bank's assets.
exp: Bankers have a fiduciary duty to preserve the bank's assets.

q: The minimum capital requirement for a commercial bank in India is ₹50 crores.
exp: The minimum capital requirement for a commercial bank in India is ₹200 crores.

q: A bank can lend up to 90% of the property's value under the mortgage policy.
exp: Banks can lend up to 80% of the property's value under the mortgage policy.

q: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meets every month.
exp: The RBI's MPC meets every quarter to set monetary policy.

q: A bank's net worth is the difference between its assets and liabilities.
opts: It depends on the bank type
exp: A bank's net worth is the difference between its equity and liabilities.

q: The RBI's Open Market Operation (OMO) involves buying and selling government securities.
exp: The RBI's OMO involves both buying and selling government securities.

q: A bank's reserve requirement ratio is 4% of its deposits.
exp: A bank's reserve requirement ratio is 4% of its deposits in India.

q: The Basel III Accord sets a minimum capital requirement of 10% for banks.
exp: The Basel III Accord sets a minimum capital requirement of 7% for banks.

q: A bank can lend to a customer up to 2 times their net worth.
exp: A bank can lend to a customer up to 2 times their net worth.

q: The RBI's Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) is used to inject liquidity into the market.
opts: It depends on the market conditions
exp: The RBI's LAF is used to inject liquidity into the market.

q: A bank's credit rating is a measure of its creditworthiness.
opts: It depends on the bank's history
exp: A bank's credit rating is a measure of its creditworthiness.

q: The RBI's Deposit Insurance Scheme (DIS) insures up to ₹1 lakh of deposits.
exp: The RBI's DIS insures up to ₹1 lakh of deposits.

q: A bank's capital adequacy ratio is calculated as net worth divided by total assets.
opts: Net worth divided by total assets
Net worth divided by total deposits
Total assets divided by net worth
exp: A bank's capital adequacy ratio is calculated as net worth divided by total risk-weighted assets.

exp: The RBI's SSW allows banks to sell securities to the RBI.

exp: A bank's ROE is a measure of its profitability.
